name: Rerau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey wordlists (Z'graggen) and Daniels 2022 subgrouping; no phonological description located

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. Website (dondaniels.weebly.com, updated 2021-09-23) and CV (c. 2021; held); Univ. of Oregon profile
sources.note: Fieldwork table lists 13 languages, Rerau not among them; CV lists only Jilim (Sgi Bara) phonetics talks (Daniels, Haupt & Baese-Berk 2020 ALS; 2021 APLL13 'The phonetics and phonology of Jilim intrusive vowels') and no Rerau publication.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG. 2007-2013. PNG Language Resources: Rerau (Internet Archive copy)
sources.note: 'Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' (live sil.org/pnglanguages.sil.org could not be reached by automated download)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pages rera1240, uppe1484, mind1258 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 0 descriptive refs; 'Comments on subclassification: Don Daniels 2022' is a comment, not a publication; AES not endangered (Ethnologue 2025: 6a Vigorous).
One-line stub; c. 590 speakers (2000 census); cites Ethnologue only.

sources.citation: OLAC. 2025. Resources in and about the Rerau language (combined catalog, 2025-11-04) + PARADISEC item records DD1-559, DD1-561, DD1-983 (Don Daniels, collector, 2016/2022)
sources.note: No language description exists in any OLAC archive. Only primary material: Daniels' PARADISEC audio -- DD1-559 'JS Wordlist 1' (2016, elicitation of Z'graggen wordlist), DD1-561 'JS Elicitation 1' (2016, basic verb and pronoun forms), and eight narrative texts DD1-983.997 recorded 2022-08-19 (audio+video). Unpublished recordings, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. (Rerau = language B22)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 7 (p. vii): transcription is 'semiphonemic.. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; fluctuation table p. viii has a Rerau row; no word on stress, accent or tone. Visual check of printed p. 3: B22 Rerau namař lam 'boy', lam duɡandu 'girl' carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1: 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing. Classification only: 'The Nuru Family consists of the languages Usu, Erima, Duduela, Kwato, Rerau, Jilim and Yangulam'; B22 Rerau 235 speakers; pronoun tables.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing (village gazetteer): B22 Rerau 235 = Rerau village 165 + Wenge 70.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Survey-wide disclaimer, sec. 1.3.3 p. 7 (p. 14): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Rerau is not a separate language here: sec. 2.4.8 p. 106 lists 'Jilim JIL (550) Villages: Alibu, Jamjam, Jilim, Rerau, Wenge'; no Rerau data.

sources.citation: Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range. PL A-23: 45-78; Ray, S. H. 1919. The languages of Northern Papua. JRAI 49: 317-341; Hanke, A. 1909. Grammatik und Vokabularium der Bongu-Sprache
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Rerau/Jilim/Wenge: no hits in any of the three; Rerau area not covered.
Lexicon from Z'graggen (1980) only; no prosodic information.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2022. Irregular sound change in the Minjim languages. Paper, 25th International Conference on Historical Linguistics (ICHL 25), Oxford. (The 'Daniels 2022' behind Glottolog's Upper Minjim subgrouping of Rerau + Sgi Bara)

sources.citation: Daniels, Don, Zoë Haupt & Melissa Baese-Berk. 2020/2021. Intrusive vowels and complex consonant clusters in Jilim (ALS 2020); The phonetics and phonology of Jilim intrusive vowels (APLL13, 2021)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Phonetic-phonological work on Sgi Bara/Jilim, Rerau's only sister in Upper Minjim (Rerau was listed as a Jilim village in 1971); likely to describe stress in the closest relative and possibly to mention Rerau. Talks only; no paper located.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don (collector). 2016-2022. Rerau materials in PARADISEC collection DD1: DD1-559 'JS Wordlist 1' (elicitation of Z'graggen wordlist), DD1-561 'JS Elicitation 1', DD1-983/985/987/989/991/993/995/997 (eight narratives, 2022-08-19)

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists at the publisher (DOI recorded); open or paywalled, not checked; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The only first-hand modern Rerau data in existence; audio (+video) of a wordlist and texts. Not a description, but a phonetician could establish the stress pattern from the wordlist recording. Access needs a PARADISEC login (catalog.paradisec.org.au could not be reached by automated download).
